title: Byzantine Churches in Constantinople
author: Alexander Van Millingen and contributors
detail: The primary survey records the externally three-sided apses, low windowless Ottoman dome, side wall levels, original central arches and replacement wooden narthex.
Architectural documentation gives the 15 by 17.5 m church plan, three polygonal apses and the Ottoman tower at the southwest corner.
Semavi Eyice describes the surviving low dome and late wooden porch, and records the reconstruction of the stone minaret cap after the earthquake.
District religious-affairs inventory records the timber narthex and right-front stone minaret with a single balcony.
The broadcaster reports the Hazreti Cabir Mosque’s reopening following its restoration in May 2024.
